final_recommendation: The room converged on a conditional settlement: FINMA funds 25% recovery by month-end with sealed discovery, bondholders sign Thursday only if Wednesday's market test (AT1 spreads compressing below 180bps) succeeds—otherwise they file Friday. The seal trades litigation silence for regulatory protection, but the AT1 market's permanent repricing (40-50bps wider) remains unresolved.
minority_objections: credit_market_analyst repeatedly warned that 25% recovery plus statement would not move peer AT1 spreads materially, predicting permanent 40-50bps widening regardless of settlement
institutional_investor demanded transparent recovery floors for future write-downs, which FINMA rejected as ultra vires constraint on emergency discretion
insurance_observer flagged that sealed discovery does not protect against parallel shareholder derivative suits once D&O carriers see board memos
key_conflicts: Bondholders demanded FINMA commit in writing to equity-subordination-first process for future AT1 write-downs; FINMA refused as legally impossible pre-commitment of sovereign discretion
Market analysts vs. legal teams: analysts insisted spreads would not revert without binding procedural gates; lawyers argued legal clarity alone should stabilize pricing

D&O coverage uncertainty: insurance_observer warned carriers would deny coverage for 'known ultra vires conduct' if March 19 memos showed board knew of hierarchy inversion; FINMA insisted memos showed lawful compliance with emergency ordinance
key_concessions: FINMA agreed to fund 25% recovery by month-end and release unredacted March 19 file Wednesday, with sealed discovery contingent on Thursday signature
FINMA committed to public statement that write-down was 'one-time emergency measure, not precedent' and that future write-downs require board sign-off on viability findings filed within 30 days
Bondholders accepted 25% recovery (down from initial 40% demand) in exchange for sealed discovery and carrier commitment letter
FINMA secured written carrier commitments that sealed discovery would not trigger D&O coverage denial through settlement period
red_lines: FINMA: will not commit in writing to recovery floors or equity-subordination-first requirements for future crises (ultra vires constraint on emergency authority)
Bondholders: will not sign silence until Wednesday market test confirms AT1 spreads compress below 180bps; retain Friday filing option if test fails
Insurance carriers (implicit): will deny D&O coverage if March 19 memos show board knew of hierarchy inversion and signed anyway, treating it as fiduciary breach with knowledge
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Parallel shareholder derivative suits once March 19 memos surface in any discovery, even if bondholder claims settle—insurance_observer raised this but room did not model the three-year D&O tail

Permanent AT1 market repricing (40-50bps wider) as structural cost-of-capital increase for all issuers, regardless of settlement—credit_market_analyst flagged this repeatedly but room treated it as exogenous
Reinsurance accumulation risk if multiple AT1 issuers face similar claims simultaneously—mentioned once by insurance_observer but not developed
Political/legislative risk that Swiss parliament could override FINMA's settlement authority or funding commitment—never surfaced despite month-end funding pledge
downstream_risk_variables: AT1 spreads Wednesday close: if Deutsche/Barclays/BNY do not compress below 180bps, bondholders file Friday and settlement collapses
D&O carrier reservation timeline: if carriers reserve coverage on March 19 memos after settlement, FINMA faces parallel three-year defense-cost litigation
Shareholder derivative suit trigger: once any discovery surfaces board minutes showing hierarchy-inversion knowledge, derivative claims spike regardless of bondholder settlement seal
Peer AT1 issuance freeze: 18-month window where no major issuer can price AT1 competitively, forcing shift to equity or Tier 2 capital
Basel Committee response: whether global regulators issue clarifying guidance on AT1 hierarchy to contain contagion, or remain silent and let market reprice permanently
uncertainty_notes: The settlement's viability hinges entirely on Wednesday's market test—whether AT1 spreads compress below 180bps after FINMA's statement and file release. If spreads do not move, bondholders file Friday and the sealed-discovery framework collapses, triggering three-year multi-jurisdictional litigation. The room never resolved whether FINMA's procedural commitments (board sign-off, 30-day filing) would actually prevent future hierarchy inversions under systemic stress, leaving the AT1 market's permanent repricing (40-50bps wider) as an unhedged tail risk. D&O carrier coverage for parallel derivative suits remains unaddressed.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the room's central forcing mechanism: bondholders threatened Friday filing in every round, secured New York counsel, filed preservation notices, and made the entire settlement conditional on Wednesday's market test—driving every concession from FINMA.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: The room built a sustained, multi-round challenge to FINMA's legal authority: demanding discovery of March 19 ordinance drafting, questioning whether FINMA knew it inverted Basel hierarchy, and structuring the settlement around proving the write-down was 'emergency-driven, not precedent-setting.'
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: The equity-preserved-while-AT1-wiped inversion was the room's core grievance and negotiating lever: every settlement term (25% recovery, procedural gates, public statement) was designed to address or contain the hierarchy-inversion precedent and its contagion to Deutsche/Barclays/BNY.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing (40-50bps permanent widening, 18-month issuance freeze, 200+bps spread widening) was a constant, decision-shaping thread: credit_market_analyst repeatedly warned the settlement would not reverse it, and institutional_investor made clear they would not hold AT1 through a three-year discovery tail.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: The multi-year claims tail was discussed seriously (three-year bondholder discovery, parallel D&O denial litigation, shareholder derivative suits) and shaped settlement terms (sealed discovery, carrier commitment letters), but it was not the dominant driver—litigation momentum and hierarchy precedent were stronger.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O exposure surfaced concretely (carrier denial for 'known ultra vires conduct,' defense-cost reservation, parallel derivative suits) and drove FINMA to secure written carrier commitments, but it remained a secondary concern—important enough to require action, not central enough to dominate the room's direction.
